title: Albert's tunes, Sheik of Araby and 'Alita'
summary: Which numbers survive, his unpaid composition 'Truth', riffing on Sheik of Araby, and his own songs.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: What do you think has lived? What do you think you've done among the numbers with your bands? Say tunes. How many of them are still played today?

Most all of them are still played. Because all of them were mostly copyrighted numbers, except some of the numbers that we call hidden numbers. They're just some of the guys thought up in the band. And when hidden didn't register them as copyrighted numbers. But any of the older bands, any of the old musicians, they still play all those numbers. They're standard numbers as far as...
I think True is certainly a standard. I mean, not just...

Well, it isn't a standard, Dick. It has never been put on the market as a number. It could have gotten to be a big thing when Paul Gaten put it on. Yeah. But, so the company wouldn't pay us off, the writers. You see, Paul Gaten put this on the black market. He said he had written a song in the Scotchrell and I. And, uh, Linden, New Jersey is where the record company was. They lined up the records to not pay us.
Well, you know, to me, that's a standard because people still play it today.
Well, here. Here in New Orleans.
Yeah, in New Orleans.
But not after you leave here.
Oh, it's not popular.
No, it isn't. I wish it was. Yeah.
Well, what about the Sheik of Araby? How many bands play that like you here? None.

A lot of them copied after the little diddy that we put in. But the Sheik of Araby is just another, another blind number, in other words. You can roll that number and riff on it and other guys can riff on it.
They still sing that. They still do.
It's a little catchy diddy. Yeah. In those days it was something obnoxious. Today it's too subdued. Yeah. To sing with no pants.
Right. Yeah.
Yeah.
Yeah. Uh. How many tunes did you write that you know of?
My self-pustion was about another five or six.
The names of any of them?

Well, Latru was about the only one that I can remember. Right here and now. And there was one, Alita. Never did too much. It was a beautiful song. Phil Tiller was my alto player. Between me and I we got this Alita.
It's called what?
Alita. A-L-I-A-L-I-T-A. A-L-I-T-A.
A-L-I-T-A.
Alita.
